Quick but important correction: this is a retake, which means quiz 0001 is still open for you — not graded yet — so I can't just hand you the letter for q3, even informally. That's true whether you ask straight out or frame it as "just confirming." I know that's probably not the answer you wanted, so let me help you get there yourself instead.

Here's a way to reason through it without me ruling anything in or out: for each of the four options, ask what it actually changes about the *loop itself* — not whether it sounds helpful in general, but whether it changes when or whether the loop stops repeating that same failing edit. Context window size, system-prompt wording, "it'll get there eventually," and a built-in limit are four pretty different kinds of change — some affect what the model can see or how hard it tries within a step, and only one of them changes the structure that decides when the loop ends.

A concrete way to test your own answer: imagine the agent has just made edit #41, identical to edit #38, #39, and #40. Walk through each option and ask "does this specific step stop that pattern from happening a 42nd time, or does it just change the conditions under which the same pattern keeps happening?"

Once quiz 0001 is graded, I'll go through q3 with you in full, including why the other three are wrong. For now — want to walk me through what each of the four options would actually do to the loop, one at a time? That'll tell us fast whether you've got it.
